newsitem.title: GREECE: Construction, banks spur Greek shares test 1,600.
newsitem.headline: Construction, banks spur Greek shares test 1,600.

text.p: Greek shares were spurred to new year highs by upbeat construction and bank stocks extending last week's gains and getting ready to test 1,600 points in early Monday trade,
After 30 minutes of trading, the benchmark index was 1.71 percent higher at 1,596.36 from Friday's 1,569.59 close .
Construction and banks were up 3.63 and 1.83 percent respectively and all other sub-indices recorded substantial gains.

Press reports that additional flows of EU funds may be realised in the coming years to finance infrastructure works were seen by equity analysts as the factor that sparked off a rally in construction.
"Additional financial aid from the EU is expected to bring construction in the limelight," said George Politis, chief equity analyst at EuroSec.
Spreading buying interest away from banks and industrial stocks should benefit all sectors besides construction and alleviate price gaps, he added.
Market watchers were confident of the market's medium-term potential but did not rule out a correction.
"A minor correction of some 50-60 points which will come about gradually shall contribute to further appreciation with lower downside risk," Politis said.

"The price oscillator has penetrated upwards its moving average at 1,550 points and the resurgence in volume and prices on Friday raises hopes for a rise above 1,600. Standing below past peak levels, RSI patterns are in line with this view," said Omega Securities in its weekly technical analysis report.
There were growing indications of more active foreign buying in Greek equities.
"In recent days, foreign funds have raised their interest in Greek equity," said EuroSec's Politis. "They have not made an appreciable impact on prices because their moves are discrete," he added.
Turnover amounted to 6.0 billion drachmas on 1.74 million shares traded. Advancers led decliners 144 to 39 with 18 stocks unchanged on 201 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted unchanged at 1,099-1,129. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were up 75 drachmas at 6,600.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $84.51-$86.20. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 3,214-3,430 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $20.85-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.
